General Provisions This Handbook is designed to provide employees with a single reference point for all information relating to their employment. Within it you will find the policies and guidelines that govern your conduct in The Company, as well as The Company’s conduct relating to your employment. This Handbook is not a contract of employment and does not create contractual entitlements beyond those provided in your Employment Agreement, Offer Letter, Appointment Letter or under applicable law. The Company’s Management may amend, alter, modify or replace any part of this Handbook from time to time

Policy and Process Equal Opportunity Policy The Company acknowledges its moral and legal obligations regarding non-discrimination at the workplace and equal opportunity in recruitment. We offer equal opportunity to all persons irrespective of disability, race, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, pregnancy, religion or similar belief. It is contrary to our value system to discriminate against any person on these grounds in the terms and conditions of employment or in opportunities for training and promotion. We recognise that equal opportunity is a continuous, ongoing process that must remain under constant review

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Recruitment - Policy and Process
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Recruitment - Policy and Process

We recognise that equal opportunity is a continuous, ongoing process that must remain under constant review. This policy reflects the principles of equal opportunity and reasonable accommodation recognised under Indian law, including the rights of persons with disabilities. Disciplinary action will be taken against any employee found to have discriminated against another employee on any of the grounds set out above, including by treating them less favourably, by harassment or victimisation, or by failing to make reasonable adjustments to prevent a disadvantage at work.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Recruitment - Policy and Process
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Recruitment - Policy and Process

• Recruitment is carried out solely on the basis of an applicant’s abilities and suitability for the role. The Company will make reasonable adjustments to its recruitment procedure to ensure applicants are not placed at a disadvantage.
• Induction: On commencement, The Company will, in consultation with the employee, take all reasonable steps to enable that employee to work safely and effectively. Where specialist expertise is required - for example, in relation to a differently-abled employee - The Company will consult an appropriate specialist.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Recruitment - Policy and Process
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Recruitment - Policy and Process

• Training and career development: All employees have equal rights to training, promotion, incentives and other aspects of career development based on their abilities. Please refer to the Training and Education Policy.
• Benefits: All employees have equal access to benefits and facilities, with reasonable adjustments made where necessary.
• Retention and adjustments: The Company will take reasonable measures to retain employees and enable them to perform their duties, which may include specialist equipment, job redesign, re-training, flexible hours or redeployment. Adjustments are arranged in consultation with the employee and reviewed at reasonable intervals.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Recruitment - Policy and Process

• Grievance redressal: Any grievance under this policy should be reported, in writing or orally, as soon as possible to the designated committee by email to complaints@insomniacs.in. Recruitment Process
• Recruitment is a competitive process. It is carried out through advertisements, job postings, conferences, applications, employee referrals and any other appropriate method.
• The minimum age for employment at The Company is 18 (eighteen) years.
• Every applicant is subject to interviews, tasks and such other requirements as may be necessary to determine suitability (“Pre-Employment Requirements”). The purpose is to understand the applicant’s skills, ability and fit for the role.

The process is complete only when the Employment Agreement is executed, the stated formalities are completed and supporting documents are provided.

content:

Working Life at The Company Probation
• On acceptance of the Offer Letter and on joining, every employee is subject to a probation period of the duration specified in their Offer Letter or Employment Agreement, calculated from the date of joining. The probation period may differ between employees and, where it does, the applicable period will be stated in the Offer Letter or Employment Agreement.
• Leave entitlement during probation is governed by the Leave Policy. Leave accrues from the date of joining but may be availed only after confirmation of employment.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Working Life at The Company
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Working Life at The Company

• The benefits available during probation and on confirmation will be outlined in the Offer Letter, Appointment Letter or Employment Agreement, as applicable.
• If The Company finds that an employee is not suited to the role during probation, it may either change the job profile or terminate the employment by serving 7 (seven) days’ written notice. If the job profile is changed at The Company’s option, the employee may accept the new role or terminate employment by serving 7 (seven) days’ written notice to the Reporting Manager, the HR department and Management (with HR marked on all related emails). The probation period for a revised job profile will be determined on a case-by-case basis.

content:

• An employee found to be in breach of the Employment Agreement, Offer Letter, Appointment Letter or this Handbook while on probation may be terminated in accordance with the disciplinary process, and for serious misconduct, without notice.
• All employees are added to official communication groups (WhatsApp / HR Application) as required and are expected to remain in them. Voluntarily leaving an official group without authorisation is treated as an act of indiscipline and may attract disciplinary action.

• Time of arrival and departure is registered in the attendance system on the HR Application. Employees must record attendance daily; failure to do so will be marked as absent for that day.

• Proxy attendance is strictly prohibited. No employee shall mark attendance on behalf of another, request another to mark attendance on their behalf, share attendance credentials, or otherwise manipulate attendance records.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Salary
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Salary

• Salaries are determined by the employee’s role and as mutually agreed between the employee and Management.
• Salary is paid in 12 monthly installments and is paid on the 7th day of each month. If the 7th is a public holiday, salary is paid one or two days earlier or later. In case of delayed payment, please contact HR immediately.
• Each employee receives an individual salary statement specifying the components of salary, statutory deductions (such as taxes and statutory contributions), insurance premiums (if any) and any other deductions you have authorised.
• Increments and promotions are not automatic and depend on the employee’s performance.

• If the referring employee separates from the company before the payout date, they forfeit eligibility for the referral bonus.
• All referrals must be submitted to the HR Department through the approved referral process/email prior to or at the time of the candidate's application, to ensure proper record-keeping and tracking.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Information Security, Acceptable Use and BYOD Policy
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Information Security, Acceptable Use and BYOD Policy

Information Security, Acceptable Use and Conditional Use (BYOD) Policy Purpose and Scope
• This Policy governs the use of Company systems, networks, applications, data and resources, and the use of personally owned devices for Company work. It is intended to protect the Company's confidential information, intellectual property, client data, digital infrastructure and operational security. It forms an integral part of this Handbook and your employment terms, and is binding on all employees, interns, consultants, contractual personnel and any other person authorised to access Company systems or data. In this Policy, "Company Data"

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Information Security, Acceptable Use and BYOD Policy
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Information Security, Acceptable Use and BYOD Policy

means any data, information or material owned by or entrusted to the Company, in any form and on any device, and "Personal Device" means any personally owned laptop, desktop, tablet, mobile phone, storage device or other electronic device used for Company work. Authorisation and Conditional Use (BYOD)

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Information Security, Acceptable Use and BYOD Policy
content:

Such permission is conditional on full compliance with this Policy and is revocable at the Company's sole discretion, including where the Company considers that a device or its use may expose it to cybersecurity, confidentiality, legal, operational, reputational or regulatory risk. An employee who does not wish to use a Personal Device may request a Company-provided device, subject to availability and role requirements. The use of a Personal Device, and the consent associated with it, is therefore voluntary. Security Compliance Obligations

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Information Security, Acceptable Use and BYOD Policy
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Information Security, Acceptable Use and BYOD Policy

Devices must not be rooted, jailbroken or otherwise security-compromised. The Company may require the installation of approved endpoint protection, VPN, monitoring, authentication or mobile-device-management (MDM) software as a condition of access. Failure to meet these obligations may result in suspension of access and disciplinary action

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Information Security, Acceptable Use and BYOD Policy

• Filing a complaint: An aggrieved person may lodge a written complaint with the IC, ideally within 3 (three) months of the incident (or the last incident in a series). • Assistance: If the complainant is unable to make a written complaint, the IC will render all reasonable assistance. Where the complainant is unable to complain due to incapacity, the complaint may be made by their legal heir, relative, friend, co-worker or any person with knowledge of the incident, in accordance with the Workplace (POSH) Act and rules.

content:

• Conciliation: Before an inquiry, the IC may - only at the request of and with the consent of the complainant - attempt to resolve the matter through conciliation. No monetary settlement may form the basis of conciliation. Conciliation should be concluded within a reasonable period; if a settlement is reached, copies are provided to both parties and the matter is closed.
• Formal inquiry: If conciliation is not opted for, fails, or its terms are not honoured, the IC will conduct a formal inquiry in accordance with the principles of natural justice. The inquiry is to be completed within 90 days as provided by the Workplace (POSH) Act.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) Policy

A complaint made in good faith that is not upheld will not attract any action against the complainant; however, a knowingly false or malicious complaint may be dealt with under the Workplace (POSH) Act.

Your Statutory Rights - Workplace Health and Safety The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 entitles you to a safe workplace, basic welfare facilities and protection from hazardous conditions. This applies equally to incidents involving a Company or personal vehicle used on Company duty.

The employee must cooperate fully and promptly with the Company and its representatives, provide complete and truthful information, and preserve any relevant records or evidence.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Travel and Associated Expense Policy
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Travel and Associated Expense Policy

Local Travel (Non-Trip, Official)
• Local travel for official purposes (office to client office and return, for business meetings) is reimbursed at actuals, subject to the caps below. Choose the most economical and time-efficient mode.
• Only ordinary taxis are reimbursed. Retain receipts or a photograph of the metered fare.
• Where local business travel is made directly to or from the employee’s home, approval with justification should be sought.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Travel and Associated Expense Policy
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Travel and Associated Expense Policy

• Late-hours safe travel: Where an employee works late at the office, The Company reimburses safe transport home at actuals on submission of a receipt or a photograph of the meter with a note of the work involved. To support the safety of all employees, this applies to any employee working until 11:00 PM or later, and The Company will arrange or reimburse safe transport for women employees working after 10:00 PM, consistent with the safeguards for night work under the relevant Acts.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Travel and Associated Expense Policy
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Travel and Associated Expense Policy

• Food at office (late working): An employee working at the office premises after 10:00 PM may claim reimbursement for food ordered after 10:00 PM at actuals, subject to a maximum of INR 250 per person per night, with a GST invoice and an approval note. Expense Reports and Travel Activity Reports
• Expense reports must be submitted in the approved format (on HR Application) to Accounts within 7 days of the end of a business trip, and within the first day of the new week for the previous week’s claims. Local-travel reimbursements are paid monthly.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Travel and Associated Expense Policy
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Travel and Associated Expense Policy

• Delayed reports may result in certain expenses (especially those without supporting documents) being disallowed. Reports not submitted within a month of the end of the journey will not be reimbursed.
• All invoices, bills and receipts must be GST-compliant. A non-GST-compliant bill is reimbursed at only 50% of its value. For rickshaw travel, a photograph of the meter showing the amount is sufficient.
• A Travel Activity Report must be submitted to the Reporting Manager, who will approve, suggest corrections or disapprove it within 1 working day. It is then sent with the Expense Report to Accounts, who act as custodian.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > HR Application
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > HR Application

• The Company uses the Bitrix24 application as its HRMS to manage key HR functions.
• To enable smooth internal management, employees are expected to install and use the HR Application on their mobile phone.
• HR Application is used to track progress and attendance, to administer policies, for record-keeping and leave applications, and similar purposes. Employees should use HR Application for communications with HR where practicable, and may use email or call where the application does not support a particular communication.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > HR Application
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > HR Application

• Clock-in / clock-out: Employees clock in and out when at the office, a meeting location or on outdoor duty. If you step out for a personal reason, clock out and clock back in on return.
• If you fail to clock in or out, you may be marked absent for that period unless the discrepancy is corrected with your Reporting Manager and HR.
• Records on HR Application are used to administer the policies in this Handbook and the Employment Agreement. Location Tracking - Consent and Limits

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > HR Application
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > HR Application

• HR Application includes location functionality used to verify attendance and field duty and to support employee safety. By using the application for work, you consent to location tracking during your working hours and while you are clocked in.
• Location tracking is limited to working hours and to periods when you are clocked in. It does not operate after you clock out or outside working hours. You are not required to keep location services on outside working hours for attendance purposes.
• Location and attendance data is collected only for the purposes stated above, is accessed only by authorised personnel, and is handled in accordance with the Data Protection section of this Handbook.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > HR Application
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > HR Application

• If you have a concern about location tracking, you may raise it with HR; The Company will address it reasonably and in line with applicable law. Why this Handbook does not ask you to “waive” your privacy Following the Supreme Court’s recognition of privacy as a fundamental right (K.S. Puttaswamy), and consistent with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, monitoring is based on informed consent, a clear purpose and proportionate limits

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > HR Application
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > HR Application

not a blanket waiver of privacy. Tracking confined to working hours, for stated purposes, is the lawful and enforceable way to achieve the Company’s operational needs. Data Protection and Employee Privacy The Company processes personal data about its employees (such as contact details, identity and bank details, attendance, performance and, where relevant, health information) for legitimate employment and statutory purposes. The Company is committed to handling this data lawfully and responsibly, consistent with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act,

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > HR Application
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > HR Application

2023. • Purpose: Employee personal data is collected and used for payroll, statutory compliance, attendance, performance management, safety and the administration of this Handbook and the Employment Agreement.
• Consent and notice: Where the law requires consent, The Company will obtain it and provide notice of the purpose. Sensitive personal data (such as health information) is handled with additional care and shared only with those who need to know.
• Access and correction: You may ask HR to access or correct your personal data held by The Company, subject to applicable law.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > HR Application
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > HR Application

• Security and retention: The Company applies reasonable security safeguards and retains personal data only for as long as necessary for the purposes above or as required by law.

content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > HR Application

• Your obligations: When you handle the personal data of colleagues, clients or third parties in the course of your work, you must do so only for authorised purposes and in accordance with this section and your confidentiality obligations. Statutory Employment Benefits The Company provides statutory employment benefits to eligible employees in accordance with applicable law. Your Statutory Rights - Social Security Provident Fund (PF): Eligible employees are enrolled in the Employees’ Provident Fund, with employer and employee contributions as prescribed, under the Code on Social Security,

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > EPF and ESI Policy
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > EPF and ESI Policy

• The Company shall comply with all applicable obligations relating to the Employees' Provident Fund and Employees' State Insurance schemes, in accordance with the provisions of applicable law.
• Eligible employees shall be enrolled in the relevant schemes, and the prescribed employee contributions shall be deducted from salary and remitted along with the employer's contributions within the statutory timelines.
• Employees shall furnish all information and documentation reasonably required for registration, nomination and claim processing.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Protection of Confidential Information and Meetings
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Protection of Confidential Information and Meetings

• The recording, circulation or publication of any content from internal meetings, client meetings, review meetings or any other official Company or client meeting is prohibited without authorisation.
• Where an employee is permitted to record a meeting or voice note for internal purposes, that person is responsible for any consequences of distributing or sharing the content outside The Company - including sharing with friends, family, the media or social media - and may face disciplinary and legal consequences.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Protection of Confidential Information and Meetings
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Protection of Confidential Information and Meetings

• Employees must not photograph, screen-record, print or photocopy Company or client information except as required for authorised work. Unauthorised photographing, recording, printing or copying may be treated as theft of intellectual property or a breach of confidentiality and dealt with under the disciplinary process and applicable law.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Protection of Confidential Information and Meetings
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Protection of Confidential Information and Meetings

• The purpose of this policy is to safeguard The Company’s integrity and protect sensitive information from misuse or unauthorised disclosure. Grievance Redressal The Company encourages employees to raise concerns early. If you have a work-related grievance, raise it first with your Reporting Manager; if it is unresolved or it would be inappropriate to raise it with your manager, escalate it to HR at hr2@insomniacs.in. Grievances relating to harassment should be raised through the POSH or Anti-Harassment routes described in this Handbook. Note

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Protection of Confidential Information and Meetings
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Protection of Confidential Information and Meetings

Grievance mechanism under the Codes The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 provides for a grievance redressal mechanism in establishments of the prescribed size. The Company maintains an internal grievance route consistent with this requirement and will constitute a Grievance Redressal Committee as and where required by the Code and the applicable rules.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Whistleblower and Protected Disclosures
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Whistleblower and Protected Disclosures

• The Company encourages employees to report, in good faith, any actual or suspected fraud, financial irregularity, corruption, bribery, theft, misuse of Company resources, breach of law or regulation, serious safety violation, or breach of this Handbook or Company policy.
• Such a disclosure may be made confidentially by email to complaints@insomniacs.in or directly to any member of Management. Disclosures may be made anonymously, although providing your identity assists investigation. The Company treats the identity of a person making a good-faith disclosure as confidential to the extent reasonably possible.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Whistleblower and Protected Disclosures
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Whistleblower and Protected Disclosures

• No employee will be subjected to dismissal, demotion, harassment, victimisation or any other detrimental treatment for making a disclosure in good faith, even if the concern later proves unfounded. Retaliation against such a person is itself treated as serious misconduct. This protection does not extend to a disclosure that the employee knows to be false or that is made maliciously, which may itself attract disciplinary action.

section_title: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Whistleblower and Protected Disclosures
content:
Section: EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK > Whistleblower and Protected Disclosures

• Concerns relating to sexual harassment should be raised through the POSH or Anti-Harassment routes set out in this Handbook. Whistleblower Investigation Procedure All disclosures received under the Whistleblower Policy shall be reviewed promptly and investigated fairly, confidentially and without retaliation against the complainant acting in good faith. Knowingly false or malicious complaints may attract disciplinary action. Appropriate corrective action shall be taken based on the findings of the investigation.
